name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District carries an R+19 partisan lean, among the most Republican seats in Georgia
Incumbent Clay Fuller was renominated and holds a heavy outside-spending edge, roughly $2.8M supporting him against minimal opposition
Polymarket prices the Republican at about 96 percent
Shawn Harris raised $8.1M but spent nearly all of it, ending with about $18K on hand and almost no outside support
model.rationale: The seat's nineteen-point Republican lean, Fuller's renomination, and a lopsided outside-spending picture outweigh Harris's large but fully spent fundraising haul; prediction markets price a Republican win near 96 percent, and no polling or expert ratings point to a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending in Harris's favor or the first public polling showing a single-digit margin would be the clearest sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 14th District sits in the state's northwest corner and carries a Republican partisan lean of roughly nineteen points, among the strongest in Georgia. Incumbent Clay Fuller, renominated without difficulty, seeks another term against Democrat Shawn Harris, a first-time challenger.

Harris posted one of the cycle's largest fundraising totals for a challenger, more than $8 million, but enters the final stretch with under $20,000 on hand after heavy spending. Outside groups have put about $2.8 million behind Fuller while directing roughly $450,000 against Harris, and almost no outside money has aired in Harris's support. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have rated it. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 96 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the outside-spending imbalance points to a comfortable Republican hold.
